summary: Misaligned embedding batch interleaving causing fluctuating rerank scores and intermittent timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports non-deterministic reranking results and occasional 504 timeouts when submitting batched embed+rerank requests from their dedicated cluster. Behavior started after they enabled 'auto-batch' on their SDK client and upgraded to open-embedder-v2-768 earlier this week.

Impact:
- DocuSearch Labs: search relevance fluctuates between requests (top results reorder unpredictably).
- Intermittent 504s observed on rerank endpoint (~1-2% of requests during peak).
- User-facing SLA degradation; customer flagged as P1.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment in us-east, serving runtime 1.18.2, batching-service 0.9.7.
- Client: docusearch-sdk v2.3.1 with auto-batch enabled.
- Model combo: embeddings (open-embedder-v2-768) followed by server-side reranker (reranker-tiny-v1) pipeline.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From customer's traffic pattern: issue appears when many concurrent sessions call /v1/embeddings in multi-item batches (sizes 8-32) followed by immediate /v1/rerank calls using the returned vectors.
2) Reproduce locally using sample harness (provided below) by enabling interleaved multi-tenant batching and replaying their header patterns.
3) Observe rerank score variance across repeated identical traces and sporadic 504s from reranker instances.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Rerank scores for identical inputs vary across calls (score deltas up to 0.12 in top-k).
- Request traces show embedding batches being interleaved incorrectly: request A's embeddings appear to be partially inserted into request B's batch metadata when forwarded to reranker.
- Reranker service sometimes returns long queue times and ultimately 504s for affected requests.

Initial hypothesis:
- Batching-service interleaves per-request vector buffers under high concurrency due to a race in buffer offset calculation after the SDK switched to a 'coalesced' prefix optimization.
- Partial corruption of per-request metadata leads to downstream reranker mixing vectors between requests, causing quality drift and timeouts when validation fails and the request is retried.

Requested customer action:
- Temporarily disable client-side auto-batch and set batch_size=1 to mitigate while we investigate.
- Provide a small redacted trace (request IDs) for two consecutive failing flows (we requested 3 trace IDs).

2026-03-12 16:05 - Marcus Lee (SRE): Reproduced a local variation of the issue using the customer's trace pattern. Observed interleaving of vector buffers in batch_forward() in dev-runner. Opening probe PR to add stricter buffer boundaries.

2026-03-12 17:30 - DocuSearch Labs (Customer) - Elena Morozova: We rolled batch_size down to 1 and saw immediate stabilization; quality now consistent. Can you confirm what changed and when a permanent fix will be available?

2026-03-13 09:12 - Marcus Lee (SRE): Patch PR 2243 created adding atomic buffer offsets and a checksum validation step on batch assembly. Running integration tests against dedicated staging. Will schedule a controlled deploy to canary cluster tomorrow morning.
investigation_notes: Checked batching-service logs for request IDs provided by customer; found overlapping memory offsets for concurrent batch assemblies at 15:14:32-15:16:18 UTC.
Heap and buffer metrics show increased live buffer reuse under high-concurrency; GC cycles correlated with timing of observed interleaving.
Added additional logging to record batch assembly start/end and per-request checksum — reproduces locally under synthetic load.
Hypothesis validated: off-by-one in the coalesced prefix length calculation causes offset drift when small padding occurs; race condition under multi-threaded assembler.
logs: trace_id=docu-20260312-01515 req=embed batch_id=ba-7790 offset_start=6000 offset_end=12144  <-- overlap detected
stack sample (batching-service): batch_forward() at assembler.cpp:278, assemble_coalesced_prefix() at assembler.cpp:189
resolution: Workaround (customer action): Disable client auto-batch or set batch_size=1. Customer confirmed stabilization after this change.

Planned fix: PR 2243 implements atomic buffer allocation and an optional per-batch checksum validation; will be rolled out to canary on 2026-03-14 and to prod (dedicated) after successful canary gating.
Follow-ups: Add a regression unit test for coalesced prefix scenarios and integration test with multi-tenant interleaved load. Add an alert for 'batch_overlap_detected' metric.
